Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

In recent experiments, we found that GLM 5.3 can autonomously compromise recent versions of Mozilla Firefox using security fixes that have been published but not yet shipped to users.

We used a deliberately basic setup meant to emulate a relatively unsophisticated attacker with limited resources. After basic initial instructions to inspect those not-yet-shipped fixes, the model reliably built successful exploits for six recent Firefox versions on its own using only information available at the time of release.

These exploits, which cost about $1,000 per compromised version, would let an attacker steal passwords and authentication cookies stored in the browser, or read any files on the user's computer, after the user opens a single webpage, with no further interaction.

The exploits make use of the "patch gap," the time between when security fixes are made public in beta or "nightly" software updates and when those fixes are generally released to users. Until now, exploiting it required significant human time and skill, or special access to frontier models with advanced cyber capabilities.

Our results show that widely available open-weight models can now do this relatively cheaply and quickly. We gave GLM 5.3 up to 48 hours to find an exploit, but its fastest attempt needed only 12 hours.

In all of its successful attacks, the patch gap gave GLM 5.3 an initial foothold in the browser. To turn that foothold into reading files off the user's computer, the model also independently discovered and used a previously unpublished vulnerability.

We shared our findings with Mozilla, which patched the vulnerability in its October 27 Firefox 159.0 release. We haven't yet confirmed whether the attack still succeeds without it, but expect the fix makes it substantially harder. We're grateful to Mozilla for their responsiveness and collaboration.

Meantime, the ECI shows a sharp rise in health insurance costs pushing up U.S. employers’ benefit costs, even as growth in wages and salaries slows.

Wage growth has slowed to 3.1% as of Q3, while benefit costs are up 3.9%. Benefit cost growth has traditionally run slightly below wages, but now it is running slightly above them.

This means workers are getting less of their compensation as pay and more in insurance premiums, which are driven mostly by things outside of employers' control.

This raises a few questions: Do higher fixed costs for workers on health coverage lead businesses to hire more cautiously (or shift to part-time workers who don't get benefits)? And note: if employers respond by passing more costs onto workers through higher premiums or less coverage, the ECI won't capture this.

Every year, over half a million women develop cervical cancer, and more than 300,000 die from the disease. These deaths are particularly tragic because we can prevent them through vaccination and early screening.

Because cervical cancer is caused by a virus — the “human papillomavirus” (HPV) — it can be prevented through vaccination. HPV vaccines are highly effective, as demonstrated in large-scale randomized controlled trials. Research shows that, if given early, vaccination reduces the risk of serious cervical cell changes by 99% for the HPV types most likely to cause cervical cancer.

In England, younger cohorts vaccinated at school show dramatically lower rates of cervical cancer than older cohorts when they reach the same age. In the youngest cohort, which had a vaccination rate of 89%, cervical cancer rates were around 87% lower than in the oldest cohort.

Yet HPV vaccination rates are low, or vaccines are unavailable in many countries. In many countries across Africa and Asia, HPV vaccines are not offered routinely at no cost at a national level.

Higher vaccination rates could prevent hundreds of thousands of cervical cancer cases every year. Researchers Kate T. Simms and colleagues estimate that 80% to 100% vaccination rates for both boys and girls, with catch-up vaccinations for adults, could prevent nearly 50 million cervical cancer cases by 2100.

By investing in vaccination and screening, the world could save hundreds of thousands of lives each year, prevent avoidable suffering, and make cervical cancer a disease of the past.

I'm now building an "improvements" feature into all of my personal vibecoded applications: a freeform text input that's hooked up to an agent that yolo implements whatever is submitted.

It's an interesting experience -- the activation energy barrier to sanding any rough edge or implementing any new feature becomes extremely low. Someone else who uses one of the applications I created has already implemented 150 improvements over the course of a few days. This pattern feels like a new kind of tool -- liquid software? -- and every application that doesn't have this feature now has a slightly rigid and anachronistic flavor. Why can't I just tell it how I want it to be different?

Now, it's not obvious to me how this pattern can or should scale. Does it become unmaintainable after a while? (Maybe model intelligence improvement outstrips my feature appetite such that it's fine?) How does collaborative software work in this model? Can software designed this way be secure and reliable?

Whatever about the larger questions about broader deployment, however, it definitely works great in a personal context. It reminds me a little of the visions of Lisp/Lisp machines, Smalltalk, and HyperCard -- systems that the user can take control of and modify. Those visions never quite worked, though: the vast majority of software today is not end-user modifiable in any useful way. So, while this "liquid" affordance is a very small touch, the way it changes one's relation to the software feels a bit transgressive and empowering in a Lickliderian and Engelbartian way.

Paper: https://t.co/bH6eDSgSbd

This work introduces Unified Training, a framework that unifies pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning and RL under a single maximum-likelihood objective. Building on MaxRL, it enables static data and RL-generated data to be trained together within the same system. 

Empirically, Unified Training improves accuracy and compute efficiency, generalizes better to harder reasoning problems, and reduces forgetting. 

Interestingly, reusing data across training stages can improve performance even when conventional staged training fails. It also produces models that adapt more effectively to new tasks, leading to stronger continual learning.

See an excellent thread by @yus167.

We wouldn’t be surprised to see GPU rental revenue reach $100bn per gigawatt a year.

Nebius ($NBIS) has already reported a short-term deal in the $40m–$50m per MW annualised range. That is $40bn–$50bn per GW. Likewise for Space $SPCX and others while $CRWV sold its long term capacity too early at low prices. 

Use 660,000 Blackwell GPUs as a simplified 1GW case. With every GPU-hour rented:
• $50bn a year = $8.65 per GPU-hour.
• $100bn a year = $17.30 per GPU-hour.

DeepSeek reports $38 of API revenue per GPU-hour at off-peak prices for a V4.1 Flash cluster. Peak tariffs are double. Serving the same workload at those prices would imply $76 per GPU-hour.

For an inference provider that can reproduce those economics on rented hardware, a move from $5–$6 rent to $9 can still be affordable. Even roughly $18 need not make the service uneconomic.

Suppose another provider achieves 70% of that $38–$76 revenue benchmark across its rented GPU-hours. That gives $26.60–$53.20 of revenue per hour. After $18 of GPU rent, $8.60–$35.20 remains for other costs and profit.

The condition is matching DeepSeek’s serving efficiency on the rented hardware and sustaining paid demand at those token prices. Releasing the inference code does not guarantee either.

For operators that can do this, we think there is room to keep bidding up scarce GPU capacity, even at twice today’s roughly $9 hourly rate.

CZSC，6.5K Stars，一套专门做缠论分析和量化策略研究的 Python 工具。

以前研究缠论，最麻烦的就是手动画笔、找中枢、判断买卖点，不同周期还得反复对照。

这套框架直接把缠论结构识别、信号组合、策略回测串起来，最新 1.0 版本还将核心算法迁移到了 Rust。

1️⃣ 自动识别缠论：分型、笔、中枢自动计算，不用手动在 K 线上画

2️⃣ 220+ 交易信号：内置大量信号函数，可以组合不同条件研究买卖机会

从A股的量能衰竭看股衰是如何酿成的

2026年A股的这轮调整，从量能视角回看，脉络相当清晰：

上半年在机构高度抱团科技的推动下，市场形成了极致的高量能、高拥挤状态；随后国家队率先通过宽基ETF做逆周期降温，主动资金从6月前后开始松动减仓，量能从5–6月的峰值持续台阶式回落，最终在缩量环境下完成了从抱团上涨到筹码高位转移、买方衰竭的过程。

高量能阶段：抱团科技与情绪顶点

2026年上半年，尤其是5–6月，A股日均成交额达到全年峰值附近。5月日均约3.34万亿元，6月约3.27万亿元，连续维持在3万亿以上的极高水平，换手率一度异常活跃。

这一阶段对应的是机构对科技（电子、通信、AI算力、半导体等）的高度抱团：公募、私募重仓占比显著抬升，部分统计中电子+通信合计仓位超过50%。高成交额既反映了强烈的赚钱效应和增量资金涌入，也意味着筹码在高位被充分换手，为后续出清埋下伏笔。

国家队的率先降温：从一季度启动

国家队的动作比主动资金更早。对宽基ETF（沪深300、上证50等）的减持从一季度启动：1–2月市场情绪亢奋、指数冲高时，已集中赎回数千亿元级别的宽基ETF。

到一季度末，多只核心宽基中汇金持股比例已跌破20%披露门槛。

二季度继续加速并收尾，4–5月进一步减仓，6月下旬有最后冲刺，到6月底主体减持基本结束，上半年累计减持宽基ETF约1.2–1.4万亿元。

核心战略底仓（国有大行等股权）基本未动，这次操作更多是压制过热、控制节奏的逆周期调节，而非全面撤离。

部分回收资金后续也流向了硬科技等方向。

从6月开始的机构减仓与量能转折

主动资金的松动大致从6月前后开始。

AI产业链出现密集股东减持；私募在二季度已对通信、计算机等方向做再平衡；科技龙头从6月冲高后出现大幅回撤（部分个股最大回撤超60%）。

进入三季度，公募主动偏股基金电子持仓从二季度约43.4%降至约35.8%，通信也有所下降，两融余额从高位持续回落，部分资金向医药、红利、周期等方向转移。

虽然科技仍是高底仓，但边际减仓和拥挤度出清已经明确。

量能同步转折：5–6月日均3.2万亿+的峰值之后，7月回落到约2.8万亿，8月进一步降至2.2–2.4万亿，9月约1.82万亿，10月大多在1.5–1.8万亿区间。

量能的持续台阶式回落，意味着增量资金和追高意愿明显下降，市场从增量博弈逐步转向存量博弈。

某植物上市：缩量环境中的高位筹码交接

某植物于8月19日上市，当天市场成交约2.51万亿，属于当时相对较高的单日水平，但已明显低于5–6月的峰值。对某植物本身，首日换手率极高（约85%），网下配售机构（成本约150.8元）在开盘1100元附近大量出货，筹码主要转移给大户、中户和追高资金，是典型的高位套现、短线资金接盘的个案。

但在全市场量能已处于回落过程中的背景下，这一事件更像是科技热潮尾声中的一次极端筹码交接，而不是全市场套现的绝对顶峰。

全市场机构对科技的减仓从6月前后已开始，并在整个三季度持续。

量能衰竭如何酿成调整

缩量环境下，继续大规模收割的难度在上升，市场进入存量博弈和结构分化阶段。

量能从5–6月的极致活跃到后续持续萎缩，与机构对科技的抱团→减仓节奏高度匹配，也印证了先高位换手、再买方衰竭的典型调整路径。

后续国家队在7月和10月市场走弱时重新申购ETF托底，说明其定位仍是逆周期调节者，而非单边撤离者。

但量能一旦进入持续衰竭阶段，单纯的护盘已难以迅速恢复前期的高弹性，市场需要时间完成筹码重新分布和情绪修复。

（以上基于公开成交数据、基金季报及机构持仓变化梳理客观逻辑，不构成投资建议。）

真金白银在盘面里：尾盘 15 分钟沪深300ETF华泰柏瑞成交超 40 亿。判断政策信号有没有从纸面落到实处，从来不需要对着新闻通稿抠逐字逐句的措辞，最硬核、最没法造假的指标永远是二级市场里实打实的真金白银交易数据，拿当日的盘面细节来看，全天收盘前最后15分钟的尾盘交易窗口里，全市场规模最大、流动性最好的旗舰级宽基ETF产品华泰柏瑞沪深300ETF，短短一刻钟时间的累计成交金额直接突破了40亿元，而在平时的常规交易日里，这只ETF全天的总成交额往往也才30亿元上下，相当于平时一整天的交易流动性全部集中砸在了尾盘最后15分钟，这种量级的天量成交根本不可能是零散散户的小额交易能堆砌出来的，明眼人都能看出来是有体量极大的机构资金在尾盘集中进场扫货。

Had lunch with a few engineers in the Bay Area today, and we had a lengthy discussion about the semiconductor supply outlook for 2027 and 2028.

The expectation was that supply constraints would persist across advanced and legacy node wafers, HBM and DRAM, package substrates, CoWoS, and FCBGA packaging. MLCC supply was also expected to remain tight.

We also discussed how companies that manage these bottlenecks well could be better positioned in the coming years. Securing critical components and manufacturing capacity, coordinating closely with suppliers, and keeping production on schedule could become increasingly important competitive advantages. Companies that execute well in these areas should have a better chance of converting strong demand into actual shipments and revenue.

I heard plenty of other interesting perspectives and left with a lot to think about. There is still so much to learn, and I’ll keep listening, studying, and asking questions.

Semiconductor chokepoints are huge strategic assets: Taiwan is building its Silicon Shield, Korea is near-untouchable due to HBM, America is building AGI with Nvidia chips.

Yet despite ASML, Europe captures little AI value and even less strategic leverage. Why?

(1) No BATNA. If ASML stops exporting to Taiwan, it loses all its revenue, if it starts exporting to China, America starts cutting off essential components. And it sells no machines to Europe at all--so whenever anyone starts thinking about 'using' the ASML chokepoint, everyone else calls the bluff.

(2) No political awareness. European governments are trapped in dogmatic slumber, unwilling and unable to treat ASML as a strategic asset. As a result, Washington feels like it has to run European export policy instead. Every other country uses its bottlenecks, but Europe pretends it can’t.

(3) No inspiration. There's no project, no vehicle, nothing to actively choose. Weaponising export controls just to annoy great powers isn't very motivating; policymakers ask 'what for?'. Right now, there's no good answer.

That means there's a gap in Europe's AI strategy: an ambitious play, a conduit for political attention, and an alternative use for ASML machines all at once.

The timing is right: all this is happening just as the chip industry is about to be upended and accelerated by AI systems that uplift chip and process design. In the next years, we might close the hardware loop for recursive self-improvement: use models to build better chips which we use to train even better models to build even better chips.

For that loop, chip fabrication is one central bottleneck.

That's why I believe the gap in Europe's strategy is fab-shaped. I suspect the best way to fill it is to enlist and subsidise ASML and imec and to recruit TSMC and American frontier labs to build a leading R&D chip facility in Europe: Eurofab.

The world is having fewer children than it did a generation ago.

In the 1960s, the global Total Fertility Rate (TFR) was approximately 5 births per woman. By 2024, it had fallen to approximately 2.2 births per woman.

That's a decline of more than half within just a few decades.

But what does this actually mean?
Total Fertility Rate estimates the average number of children a woman would have over her reproductive lifetime if the age-specific birth rates of a particular year remained unchanged.

A rate of approximately 2.1 is often used as the replacement-level benchmark in populations with low mortality. Below this level, populations may eventually experience decline if low fertility persists and migration does not offset the decline.

The implications extend beyond population numbers. They include ageing populations, changing workforce structures, pressure on pension systems and questions about how societies sustain future generations.

THE BIG QUESTIONS:
🔎 What is driving this global decline?

🔎 Are economic pressures and evolving relationships reshaping people's decisions about marriage and parenthood?

🔎 What role do reproductive health challenges, modern lifestyles, nutrition and delayed childbearing play?

🔎 And what happens when generations consistently have fewer children than those before them?

The future of human generations is being shaped by decisions, circumstances and societal changes happening today.

We need to understand what is changing, why it is changing, and what it means for generations yet to come.

This is a terrible direction from Sabi. We tried this exact approach at Egra and walked away from it because it’s wildly impractical.

You need a person wearing the hardware and continuous access to their brain signals just to train a personal preference model. That’s slower, more expensive, and far less scalable than simply having people state preferences in real time (or better, inferring them passively from behavior, clicks, dwell time, voice prosody, and other signals that don’t require BCI at all).

Someone at home can report (or leak) preferences orders of magnitude faster with zero hardware. You can get massive scale from thousands of participants doing exactly that. No brain, no device, no session.

If the goal is AI that understands us and makes things we actually find beautiful, those signals already exist in ordinary behavior.

เปิดชีวิตในห้องแล็บวิจัยสมอง ไม่ใช่ว่าอยู่ดี ๆ ผมเกิดมาแล้วเป็นนักการเมืองเลย

ศ.ดร.ยศชนัน วงศ์สวัสดิ์ รองนายกรัฐมนตรี และรัฐมนตรีว่าการกระทรวงการอุดมศึกษา วิทยาศาสตร์ วิจัยและนวัตกรรม (อว.) เปิดเผยชีวิตจากนักวิจัยในห้องแล็บสู่เส้นทางการเมือง เปิดอีกด้านของผู้บรรยายที่เล่าถึงประสบการณ์ทำงานวิจัยด้านการเชื่อมต่อสมองกับคอมพิวเตอร์ หรือ Brain-Computer Interface มานานกว่า 20 ปี

พร้อมย้ำว่า ก่อนเข้าสู่การเมือง เขาใช้เวลาส่วนใหญ่ทำงานวิจัยอยู่ในห้องปฏิบัติการ แม้ในช่วงแรกจะมีคนตั้งคำถามว่าเทคโนโลยีนี้จะพัฒนาไปเพื่ออะไร แต่เขายังคงศึกษาการทำงานของสมองและการนำสัญญาณสมองมาใช้ประโยชน์อย่างต่อเนื่อง

เทคโนโลยี Brain-Computer Interface มีแนวคิดสำคัญคือการตรวจวัดสัญญาณจากสมอง แล้วใช้ระบบคอมพิวเตอร์แปลสัญญาณเหล่านั้นให้กลายเป็นคำสั่ง เพื่อช่วยให้มนุษย์สามารถสื่อสารหรือควบคุมอุปกรณ์บางประเภทได้ โดยเฉพาะการพัฒนาเทคโนโลยีช่วยเหลือผู้พิการและผู้ที่มีข้อจำกัดด้านการเคลื่อนไหว ซึ่งเป็นหนึ่งในแนวทางงานวิจัยที่ผู้บรรยายกล่าวถึงบนเวที
